name: Ants in Leaves
description: Tree is a connected graph without cycles. A leaf of a tree is any vertex connected with exactly one other vertex. You are given a tree with n vertices and a root in the vertex 1 . There is an ant in each leaf of the tree. In one second some ants can simultaneously go to the parent vertex from the vertex they were in. No two ants can be in the same vertex simultaneously except for the root of the tree. Find the minimal time required for all ants to be in the root of the tree. Note that at start the ants are only in the leaves of the tree.
input_specification: The first line contains integer n ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 5·10 5 ) — the number of vertices in the tree. Each of the next n - 1 lines contains two integers x i , y i ( 1 ≤ x i , y i ≤ n ) — the ends of the i -th edge. It is guaranteed that you are given the correct undirected tree.
output_specification: Print the only integer t — the minimal time required for all ants to be in the root of the tree.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 622E — Ants in Leaves [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
